title: Refine prefetch strategy and adaptive page-windowing for tenant metrics queries
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Console Dashboard query p95/p99 for tenant-heavy queries (time-series and top-k) spikes during ad-hoc explorations. Current pagination model fetches fixed page-size + naive prefetch (next page only) which causes many small reads, high read-amplification, and cold first-page latency for new tenants.

Goal: Implement an adaptive page-windowing and tenant-aware prefetch strategy that reduces p99 latency for first-page and subsequent page fetches while bounding read-amplification and memory usage on backend nodes. Aim for ~25-40% reduction in p99 for common dashboard queries and <15% additional read IOPS on average.

Scope: Backend Console query API + caching layer in query service (console-query), instrumentation/metrics, and a small Console rollout flag. Does not include client-side UI changes beyond enabling header that signals query scope (already available).

Constraints and non-goals: We cannot require schema changes in the metrics store. Must operate within existing shard/partitioning scheme. Avoid increasing GC pressure or unbounded memory growth on the query node. This ticket does not implement cross-tenant shared cache (future work).
approach: 1) Replace fixed single-page prefetch with adaptive page-windowing: measure real-time access patterns per request (page index, time between page requests, tenant QPS) and compute a dynamic window (W) of pages to prefetch. 2) Tenant-aware heuristics: for low-activity tenants, prefetch conservative (W=1); for high-activity tenants or recent repeated scans, increase W up to a configured cap (W_max=4). 3) Prefetch prioritization: fetch in-order pages lazily and prioritize pages most likely to be requested next using exponential decay on historical access frequency. 4) Backpressure & budget: limit concurrent prefetch requests per-node and per-tenant to avoid IOPS spikes. 5) Cache eviction: use a two-tier LRU where prefetched pages have a slightly lower priority than explicitly requested pages. 6) Sampling and early-exit: if prefetch latency exceeds threshold or cluster is under heavy load, disable aggressive prefetch for that tenant for a cooldown period.
design_notes:
- Data model: reuse existing page cache key format: tenantId:queryFingerprint:pageCursor. No schema migration.
- Metrics: add histogram for prefetchLatency_ms, counter for prefetchRequests, gauge for activePrefetchWindowPerTenant.
- Memory: enforce per-node prefetch memory cap (configurable, default 256MB). Prefetch pages are sampled to compressed representation when possible.
- Query planner: introduce a small optimizer that consults tenant activity store (approximate counters in Redis) to decide W. The estimator will use sliding-window QPS and recent page-scan ratio.
- Safety: include feature-flag gated rollout and AB test buckets.
- Edge cases: long-running analytical queries that scan many pages will be rate-limited and fall back to streaming endpoint.
experiments:
- A/B trial on 2% of tenants with varied W_max (2, 3, 4) for two weeks.
- Canary run on staging using synthetic tenants with hot scan patterns.
- Microbenchmarks: measured first-page cold fetch vs adaptive prefetch on sample dataset of 10k tenants.

Preliminary results (staging):
- First-page p50: 40ms -> 30ms (25% improvement)
- First-page p99: 820ms -> 540ms (34% improvement)
- End-to-end p99 for multi-page scans: 1.8s -> 1.35s (25% improvement)
- Avg prefetch IOPS: +8% (within budget).

Notes: edge tenant with very high cardinality vectors saw temporary IOPS burst; added per-tenant cooldown heuristic in subsequent run.
acceptance_criteria: First-page p99 for dashboard queries reduced by >=25% over baseline in production AB test
Average additional read IOPS due to prefetch < 15% across A/B segment
No increase in OOM/GC incidents traced to prefetch memory usage in canary nodes
Feature-flagged rollout with ability to disable per-tenant
Dashboard telemetry: prefetchRequests, prefetchLatency_ms, prefetchHitRate available in console
